title: Face-localized chart presentation and logification of a split sharpening
statement:
Let $(X,M,\alpha)$ be a locally Noetherian fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth] and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Suppose a chart $c:Q\to M$ is given on a pointed etale neighbourhood of $\bar x$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, def-weil-etale-morphism], where $Q$ is a fine saturated commutative monoid, written additively. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $L=M_{\bar x}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and let $\beta:Q\to(A,\cdot)$ be the composite of the chart germ with the structural map. Define $F=\beta^{-1}(A^\times)$, $R=\{q-f:q\in Q,\ f\in F\}\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$, and $U=F^{\rm gp}\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$. Then $F$ is a face (a submonoid such that $a+b\in F$ implies $a,b\in F$). The chart germ extends uniquely to $\lambda:R\to L$, and the induced maps give isomorphisms
$$R\oplus_U A^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}L,\quad [r,u]\longmapsto\lambda(r)u,\qquad P:=R/U\xrightarrow{\iota\,\sim}L/A^\times=\overline M_{\bar x}.$$
Here $R/U$ identifies elements differing by addition of an element of $U$, and the pushout identifies $v\in U$ with $\beta(v)\in A^\times$, where $\beta$ is extended by inverting $F$. Suppose $s:P\to R$ is a monoid section of the quotient $\pi:R\to P$ and $(p,v)\mapsto s(p)+v$ is an isomorphism $P\oplus U\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ restricting to the inclusion on $U$. Then $h=\lambda s$ satisfies
$$(\alpha h)^{-1}(A^\times)=\{0\},\qquad P\oplus A^\times\xrightarrow{\sim}L,\quad (p,u)\longmapsto h(p)u.$$
In particular $P\oplus_{(\alpha h)^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times\to L$ is the associated-log-stalk isomorphism, and the map on the characteristic induced by $h$ is precisely $\iota$.

proof.text: The stalk chart hypothesis hc evaluated at the given pointed neighbourhood is already surjectivity of g.coprod j together with its exact divisorialChartCongruence kernel, where g is the chart germ and j is unitsIn. Thus no associated-log sheafification theorem is needed. The log axiom gives uniqueness of a log element whose structural image is a specified ring unit, using reflectsUnits and unitsBijective. Products mapping to units have both factors mapping to units, so F is a face.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, printed p.69: etale chart conventions; associated-log stalk formula supplied by the cited existing node.

proof.text: Construct the canonical map i:Q -> R inside Qgp and make it an F.LocalizationMap. Its units are represented by f and f^-1, its surjectivity is the defining fraction representation of R, and injectivity of Q -> Qgp gives its equality condition. The log axiom makes g(F) units. Mathlib Submonoid.LocalizationMap.lift gives ell:R -> L extending g, and epic_of_localizationMap proves uniqueness. By subgroup closure induction every element of U is a fraction of two face elements, giving the inclusion U -> R.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98: localization and sharpening definitions; agent calculation.

proof.text: Let D be the original chart congruence, B its quotient, C the localized pushout congruence, and T its quotient. The original chart kernel and surjectivity give eB:B equiv L by the monoid first isomorphism theorem. The map Q times A-units -> T sends each D-generator to a C-generator, so descends to k:B -> T. Set d=k composed with eB inverse. On Q and ring units d has the prescribed pair formulas. By the localization epimorphism property d composed with ell sends r to [r,1]. Hence d(ell(r)j(a))=[r,a]. Conversely C is contained in the kernel of ell.coprod j because the log axiom identifies each generator with its unit image. These facts prove equality of the kernel with C; surjectivity follows from the original chart. The first isomorphism theorem yields the pinned eT:T equiv L.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98: localization and sharpening definitions; agent calculation.

proof.text: Write P=R/U with quotient pi. The map Q -> P kills F. It and the trivial map on ring units descend through B to d:L -> P. On Q it is pi composed with i; on ring units it is 1. Localization uniqueness gives d composed with ell = pi. Every log unit comes from a ring unit, so d kills all log units. If ell(r) and ell(r prime) are associated, applying d proves pi(r)=pi(r prime). Conversely equality in R/U gives v in U with rv=r prime in Qgp, hence in R; ell(v) is a unit since U is a group. Thus ell(r) and ell(r prime) are associated. Surjectivity onto Associates L follows from the original chart. The monoid first isomorphism theorem yields the specified iota:P equiv Associates L.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98: localization and sharpening definitions; agent calculation.

proof.text: For a section s, the characteristic formula gives Associates.mk(ell(s(p)))=iota(p). If its structural image is a unit then reflectsUnits makes ell(s(p)) a unit, so iota(p)=1 and injectivity gives p=1. Conversely p=1 maps to 1 under every monoid homomorphism.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98: localization and sharpening definitions; agent calculation.

proof.text: Let bU:U -> A-units be the unit-valued lift of alpha composed with ell on U. For the given splitting eSplit, define H(r,a)=(p,bU(v)a), where (p,v)=eSplit inverse r. The pinned splitting gives eSplit inverse(s(p))=(p,1) and eSplit inverse(v)=(1,v). Each C-generator therefore has equal H-images, so H descends to J:T -> P times A-units. The map I(p,a)=[s(p),a] satisfies JI=id by the first formula. For IJ=id, decompose r=s(p)v and use the C-relation [v,1]=[1,bU(v)]. Thus I is an isomorphism. Composing with eT gives exactly (p,a) -> ell(s(p))j(a).

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98: localization and sharpening definitions; agent calculation.

proof.text: For h=ell composed with s, step 5 implies that every generator (p,1)~(1,a) of its associated-log congruence has p=1; its structural equation then gives a=1. The product map of step 6 is bijective, so its kernel equals that congruence, and the first isomorphism theorem gives the pinned associated-log quotient isomorphism. Finally Associates.mk(h(p))=iota(pi(s(p)))=iota(p), as already established in step 5.
